title: Who Depends on Whom?
covers: how two quantities change together, and how to name the independent variable (the input you choose) and the dependent variable (the output that responds)
cert: naming independent and dependent variables and saying which quantity depends on which

intro.caption: Lesson 9-1 — relationships between two variables. Mars Colony Alpha is growing. New crew members are coming, and the oxygen tanks are draining faster. The kid crew must name what depends on what. Three gates and a boss stand between them and the answer.

balloons.t: Two new crew members land next week. Our oxygen tanks are already draining faster. I need to know what depends on what.
Beep-beep-boop. (Screen: I brought a rock. It depends on nothing.)
Four crew, eight canisters a day. More crew means more oxygen used.
Easy. The number of crew depends on the oxygen. More oxygen made more people show up!

pages.caption: Takoda swapped them. The Commander CHOOSES how many crew come. The oxygen used RESPONDS. Ask: which one did somebody choose, and which one changed because of it?

balloons.t: Both numbers go up together. That's a relationship! Now, which one is the input?
I chose the grow-light hours for each tray. Then I just waited and measured.
I put the readings in a table. Input in the first column. Output in the second.
So the input is the crew. The oxygen is what comes out.
Now a dust storm. The panels make less power. Is that a relationship too?
BEEP-BEEP! (Screen: Battery used depends on rocks carried. I regret nothing.)

win.caption: The independent variable is the one that is chosen or changes on its own. The dependent variable changes in response. Check it with a sentence: the oxygen used depends on the number of crew members.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Name the Variables
gates.prompt: Commander Okafor chooses how many crew members live in the colony. Each day, the crew uses oxygen canisters. More crew members means more canisters are used.
hints: Conceptual: the independent variable is the one somebody chooses or that changes on its own. The dependent variable changes because of it.
Procedural: try both sentences: "___ depends on ___." Keep the one that makes sense in real life.

steps: Practice: Takoda chooses how far to fly the drone. The battery it uses changes with the distance.
Takoda chose the distance, so distance is the independent variable.
The battery used responds, so it is the dependent variable: battery used depends on distance flown.
worked.q: In "water used depends on the number of showers," which is the independent variable?

options.t: Liters of water in the greenhouse
options.fb: The greenhouse water is not part of this story. Look for the two quantities that change together: crew and oxygen.

options.t: Number of crew members
Oxygen canisters used each day
options.fb: That is Takoda's swap. The canisters used change BECAUSE the crew changes, so they are the dependent variable.

items.q: Which sentence is in the correct order?

options.t: The number of crew members depends on the oxygen canisters used.
options.fb: Backwards. Nobody picks the crew by counting canisters. The Commander chooses the crew; the canisters respond.

options.t: The crew and the oxygen do not depend on each other.
options.fb: They change together: more crew members use more canisters. That is a relationship.

options.t: The oxygen canisters used depend on the number of crew members.
The oxygen canisters used depend on the dust storm.
options.fb: The storm is not one of the two quantities here. The canisters change when the number of crew changes.

gates.pass: "Oxygen used depends on the number of crew." Idris saves it. Takoda says he meant that all along.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Cause and Effect
gates.prompt: Leilani chooses how many hours of grow light each tray gets. After 3 weeks she measures how tall the bean plants grew. Meanwhile, Pebble carries rocks home. The more rocks in its scoop, the more battery the trip uses.
hints: Conceptual: the cause is the independent variable. The effect, the thing you measure after, is the dependent variable.
Procedural: ask "Did someone choose this, or did it just happen because of the other one?" The one that just happened is dependent.

steps: Practice: Esme turns the heater dial higher, and the dome gets warmer.
Esme chose the dial setting. That is the cause, the independent variable.
The dome temperature responded. That is the effect, the dependent variable.
worked.q: Idris changes the antenna height, and the signal gets clearer. Which is dependent?

items.q: In Leilani's test, which is the dependent variable?

options.t: Height of the bean plants
Hours of grow light
options.fb: Leilani chose the hours. A quantity that is chosen is the independent variable.

options.t: The number of trays
options.fb: Leilani did not change the number of trays. The two quantities that change together are light hours and plant height.

items.q: On Pebble's trips, which is the dependent variable?

options.t: Number of rocks in the scoop
options.fb: That is the swap. Pebble chooses how many rocks to carry. The battery used is what responds.

options.t: Color of the rocks
options.fb: Rock color does not change with the battery. Look at the two quantities that change together.

options.t: Battery used on the trip

gates.pass: Tallest beans got the most light. And yes, Pebble, the rocks really do drain your battery.

gates.title: Gate 3 · The Table of Values
gates.prompt:
Idris made a table of values for the colony's oxygen. The input is the independent variable. The output is the dependent variable.
Crew members (input)Oxygen canisters used each day (output)
24
36
48
hints: Conceptual: in a table of values, the input column holds the independent variable and the output column holds the dependent variable.
Procedural: look how the output changes each time the input goes up by 1 crew member. Keep that pattern going.

steps: Practice table: rovers on a trip (input) and wheels to check (output): 1 → 6, 2 → 12, 3 → 18.
Each rover adds 6 wheels, and each output is 6 times the input.
So 4 rovers → 4 × 6 = 24 wheels. The wheels depend on the number of rovers.
worked.q: With that table, how many wheels for 5 rovers?

items.q: Why is "Crew members" in the input column?

options.t: It is the bigger number.
options.fb: Size does not decide it. The output numbers are actually bigger here.

options.t: It is the independent variable: the Commander chooses it.
It depends on the oxygen used.
options.fb: That's backwards. The oxygen used depends on the crew, so oxygen goes in the output column.

items.label: Output for 5 crew members:
items.aria: oxygen canisters used each day by 5 crew members

fb.msg: 7 is 5 + 2. Look again: 2 crew use 4, 3 crew use 6. Each output is 2 TIMES the input.
2.5 is 5 ÷ 2. More crew means MORE oxygen, so the output should be bigger than 5.
Count up from 4 crew: one more crew member adds 2 canisters, not 1.

items.fbDefault: Each crew member uses 2 canisters a day. How many for 5 crew members?

gates.pass: Five crew, ten canisters a day. Esme orders two more tanks before the new crew lands.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Storm Mystery
gates.prompt:
Three clues. A dust storm covers the solar panels. The thicker the dust, the less power the panels make. And here is Pebble's battery table.
Rocks in Pebble's scoop (input)Battery units used on the trip (output)
15
210
315
hints: Conceptual: in every relationship, one quantity changes first (the cause), and the other responds (the effect).
Procedural: write the sentence "___ depends on ___" for each clue. The quantity after "depends on" is the independent variable.

steps: Practice clue: the longer Leilani runs the water pump, the more water fills the tank.
Pump time changes first. Water in the tank responds.
So water in the tank depends on pump time. Pump time is independent; water is dependent.
worked.q: "Cold outside makes the heaters use more power." Which is independent?

items.q: Clue 1 · In the storm, which is the independent variable?

options.t: Power the panels make
options.fb: The power drops BECAUSE of the dust. A quantity that responds is the dependent variable.

options.t: Number of crew members
options.fb: The crew is not part of this clue. Look at dust and power.

options.t: Thickness of dust on the panels

items.q: Clue 2 · Takoda says, "More oxygen used made more crew members come." What is wrong?

options.t: Nothing. That is correct.
options.fb: Look at who chooses. The Commander chooses the crew, so the crew comes first, not the oxygen.

options.t: He swapped the variables. The oxygen used depends on the crew.
Crew and oxygen are not related at all.
options.fb: They are related: Idris's oxygen table shows more crew uses more canisters. Takoda just put them in the wrong order.

options.t: He should say the dust depends on the crew.
options.fb: Dust is a different clue. In this one, the quantities are crew and oxygen.

items.label: Clue 3 · Pebble brings back 7 rocks. Battery units used:
items.aria: battery units used when Pebble carries 7 rocks

fb.msg: 12 is 7 + 5. The table shows each rock uses 5 units, so the output is 5 TIMES the number of rocks.
20 is the next row after 15. For 7 rocks, keep going until the input is 7.
1.4 is 7 ÷ 5. More rocks use MORE battery, so the output must be bigger than 15.

items.fbDefault: Each rock in the scoop uses 5 battery units. How many for 7 rocks?

gates.pass: Mystery solved: dust drains the power, crew drains the oxygen, and rocks drain Pebble. Pebble still wants the rocks.

journal.heading: Lesson 9-1 — what the colony mystery taught us
rows: The quantity someone chooses, or that changes first. The Commander chooses the number of crew members.
The quantity that changes in response. The oxygen canisters used respond to the crew.
Say "the (dependent) depends on the (independent)." Oxygen used depends on crew — never crew depends on oxygen.
The input column holds the independent variable. The output column holds the dependent variable: 2 crew → 4 canisters.
Swapping the two. Ask: who chose it, and what changed because of it?
journal.quote: "Battery used depends on rocks carried. Rocks carried depends on how cool the rock is." — Pebble (via Idris's screen)

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 9-1 (Explore Relationships Between Two Variables) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: recognizing two quantities that change together, naming the independent and dependent variables, the "depends on" sentence check, and input/output columns in a table of values.
standards: Use variables to represent two quantities that change in relationship to one another; write an equation for the dependent variable in terms of the independent variable; analyze the relationship using graphs and tables
